card.title: Nintendo Switch PI3USB30532 and M92T36 Diagnostic and Repair Guide

claims.statement: Pin 5 of M92T36 is an input line that should measure between 3V to 6V, and 0V or less indicates a short on that line.
claims.evidence: Voltage measurement on pin 5 or its connecting capacitor.
claims.quote: In that pin you are supposed to have 3v to 6v. If you have 0v or less, you have a short on that line, since pin 5 is an input line, the short comes back from that line.

claims.statement: Pin 6 of M92T36 is the output voltage line and should measure between 3V to 6V, and 0V indicates a bad M92T36 chip.
claims.evidence: Voltage measurement on pin 6 or its connecting capacitor.
claims.quote: Now you need to check the output voltage that is pin 6... and its suppose to have between 3v to 6v. 0v in pin 6 means M92T36 is bad.

claims.statement: The M92T36 chip negotiates power through the USB-C port, which handles charging and HDMI video out.
claims.quote: M92T36 chip is responsible for negotiating power through the USB-C port, which happens to also be the port through which HDMI out video passes through.

claims.statement: Pin 2 of the M92T36 (VSTR/ATST2) measures battery voltage and charge; failing to receive an analog signal can cause the system to freeze in a loop.
claims.evidence: Observed behavior when pin reads unknown values.
claims.quote: pin 2 of the chip labelled VSTR/ATST2 is responsible for "Analog TEST/ Debug Pin2", it looks like this pin s responsible for measuring the battery voltage and thus its charge.

claims.statement: If payload injection via hekate fails, the PI3USB30532 is likely bad or the CPU is dead.
claims.evidence: Troubleshooting outcomes following RCM payload attempts.
claims.quote: If even the payload method failed, you probably will have a PI3USB30532 bad or the CPU is just dead af.

claims.statement: Ferrite filters and passives around the PI3USB30532 must be checked for uniform continuity and impedance when troubleshooting dock video output issues.
claims.evidence: Continuity and impedance checks with a meter.
claims.quote: Check around the passives around PI3USB. In particular the ferrite filters. These aren’t the strongest! Bell them with a meter / check impedance / continuity is uniform with all of them

procedure: Put the main board back in the switch frame and connect the battery.
Set the multimeter to DC Voltage.
Place the black probe to a ground and touch pin 5 or its connected capacitor of the M92T36 to verify 3V to 6V.
Check output voltage on pin 6 or its connected capacitor to verify 3V to 6V.
Visually inspect the screen ribbon cable, backlight ribbon cable, and connectors.
Attempt to enter RCM mode and inject the latest hekate payload if the console does not display image.
Inspect the PI3USB30532 chip pin pads and check coil continuity in parallel but not in cross.
Remove the back case and motherboard using hot air soldering tools with flux when replacing a broken charging port.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Probing live pins with standard thick multimeter probes risks slipping and causing shorts; use fine tips or a soldered paper pin.
card.caveats: Console behavior and version-specific workarounds like firmware 7.x.x procedures apply strictly based on software state.
